model.name: Cinque v2
model.notes: On openpilot master 2026-09-11 (PR #38850). Vision base b9facbcc, history in the graph, no residual head.

public_open_loop.condition: Measured. comma's public two-camera segments (openpilot CI data), native intrinsics and the device's own calibration, both cameras; every model on the same decoded frames. Truth is what the recording car did next: carState speed and acceleration, yaw rate from the device's cameraOdometry. Segments where the car never moves have no data. 45 segments from 23 cars (39 with movement).

metrics.label: Lateral error at the model's own best lag
Lateral correlation with the car's later motion
Lateral gain (1 = same size as the car's motion)

public_closed_loop.condition: Measured. comma's worldmodel-4B generates each next frame at 5 Hz from 9 history frames, 5 recorded anchor frames and the car's pose; the model drives comma's ideal car (the requested curvature and acceleration happen at once) for 7.2 s from the recorded start. Distance is to the recording car's own path. Seeds 0 and 1, averaged per segment.

truck_open_loop.condition: Measured. The G55's recorded drives replayed as the truck runs the model: narrow camera only, road-plane warp to 1.45 m (plane:1.45). Truth is the truck's CAN speed and yaw rate. Window = unit.

truck_closed_loop.condition: Measured. worldmodel-4B as in the public closed loop, but the model drives a simulation of the G55's measured steering and powertrain response instead of the ideal car. Lane-following windows from the G55's drives, day and night; distance is to the driver's recorded path; seeds 0 and 1, averaged per window.

truck_recovery.condition: Measured. The truck closed loop with a disturbance while the model drives; only the tests listed ran.

limits: Open-loop scores compare a model's action with what the recording driver or car did; a model that drives differently but well is scored as wrong, and smoother, later actions (what comma's RL residual produces by design) score worse here. Measured on the 2026-10-27 deep dive: open-loop accuracy did not predict closed-loop driving.

Closed-loop numbers come from a generative world model, not a car. Nothing separates models before about 2 s; past about 4 s the recorded anchor frames pull every model back toward the recorded path, so 4 s is the primary horizon.
Intervals are 95% percentile bootstraps over units (segments or windows); segments from the same car are not independent, so the public intervals are somewhat narrow.
Paired deltas are model minus baseline on the units both have; wins count units where the model is better in the metric's direction.
